seo.title: 30 Security Mistakes DeFi Developers Make
seo.description: Avoid these 30 common security mistakes that DeFi developers make. From oracle manipulation to flash loan attacks, learn what leads to exploits.

content.intro: DeFi protocols are high-value targets. These common mistakes have led to billions in losses. Learn from others' failures to build more secure protocols.

sections.heading: Oracle Mistakes
sections.description: Price oracle vulnerabilities that lead to manipulation.

items.title: Using spot prices from DEXes
items.description: Using instantaneous spot prices from AMMs allows flash loan manipulation to move prices within a single transaction.
items.impact: Attackers drain funds through price manipulation
items.prevention: Use Chainlink or TWAP oracles. Never rely on single-block spot prices.

items.title: No staleness check on oracle data
items.description: Using stale oracle prices when Chainlink hasn't updated in hours or days.
items.impact: Incorrect prices lead to bad liquidations or arbitrage
items.prevention: Check updatedAt timestamp. Reject prices older than acceptable threshold.

items.title: Missing oracle fallback
items.description: Protocol breaks completely when primary oracle fails or returns zero.
items.impact: Protocol freeze or incorrect behavior during oracle downtime
items.prevention: Implement fallback oracles or safe failure modes.

items.title: Ignoring oracle decimal differences
items.description: Assuming all Chainlink feeds have 8 decimals when some have different precision.
items.impact: Orders of magnitude errors in price calculations
items.prevention: Always check feed decimals and normalize to consistent precision.

items.title: Single oracle dependency
items.description: Trusting one oracle source without cross-validation for critical operations.
items.impact: Oracle compromise breaks entire protocol
items.prevention: For critical operations, cross-reference multiple oracle sources.

items.title: Governance votes based on current balance
items.description: Allowing votes based on token balance at time of vote enables flash loan governance attacks.
items.impact: Attacker passes malicious proposals with borrowed voting power
items.prevention: Use snapshot voting. Require tokens held for minimum time before voting.

items.title: Rewards based on deposit amount without time lock
items.description: Distributing rewards proportional to deposits without lockup allows flash loan reward stealing.
items.impact: Attackers claim disproportionate share of rewards
items.prevention: Require deposits to be present for multiple blocks before earning rewards.

items.title: Share price manipulation on first deposit
items.description: First depositor can donate tokens to inflate share price, griefing subsequent depositors.
items.impact: Early depositors extract value from later depositors
items.prevention: Implement virtual shares or send initial deposit to dead address.

items.title: Collateral value from manipulable source
items.description: Using AMM liquidity token value based on reserves allows collateral manipulation.
items.impact: Attackers borrow more than collateral is worth
items.prevention: Use manipulation-resistant LP token pricing or don't accept LP as collateral.

items.title: Liquidation triggers based on spot price
items.description: Liquidation decisions using spot prices allow predatory liquidations via price manipulation.
items.impact: Healthy positions liquidated through temporary price manipulation
items.prevention: Use TWAP for liquidation triggers. Add liquidation delay.

items.title: State updates after external calls
items.description: Updating balances or state after making external calls violates checks-effects-interactions.
items.impact: Attacker re-enters and exploits stale state
items.prevention: Always update state before external calls. Use ReentrancyGuard.

items.title: Missing reentrancy guard on withdraw
items.description: Withdraw functions making ETH transfers without reentrancy protection.
items.impact: Classic reentrancy drain attack
items.prevention: Add ReentrancyGuard modifier to all functions with external calls.

items.title: Cross-contract reentrancy blind spots
items.description: Only checking single contract reentrancy when protocol has multiple contracts sharing state.
items.impact: Attacker re-enters through different contract in same protocol
items.prevention: Use global reentrancy lock across all protocol contracts.

items.title: ERC-777 callback reentrancy
items.description: Accepting any ERC-20 without considering ERC-777 tokens have transfer hooks.
items.impact: Reentrancy through token transfer callbacks
items.prevention: Use ReentrancyGuard or whitelist accepted tokens.

items.title: Read-only reentrancy in view functions
items.description: View functions returning stale data when called during reentrancy.
items.impact: External protocols that read state during attack get wrong values
items.prevention: Be aware of what external protocols might read. Document reentrancy behavior.

sections.heading: Math and Logic Mistakes
sections.description: Calculation errors and business logic flaws.

items.title: Division before multiplication
items.description: Order of operations causing precision loss. Dividing before multiplying loses precision.
items.impact: Small amounts round to zero, value leakage over time
items.prevention: Always multiply before divide. Use higher precision intermediates.

items.title: Rounding always favoring users
items.description: Rounding in a direction that allows users to extract dust amounts repeatedly.
items.impact: Slow drain through rounding exploitation
items.prevention: Round in favor of the protocol for withdrawals, in favor of users for deposits.

items.title: Unchecked array operations
items.description: Loops over unbounded arrays that can grow beyond gas limits.
items.impact: Function becomes uncallable, funds stuck
items.prevention: Bound array sizes or use pagination for large datasets.

items.title: Integer overflow in fee calculations
items.description: Fee percentage times amount overflowing before division.
items.impact: Wrong fees charged or underflow to huge values
items.prevention: Check for overflow even with Solidity 0.8. Use unchecked carefully.

items.title: Missing slippage protection
items.description: Swaps without minimum output parameter allowing sandwich attacks.
items.impact: Users receive much less than expected due to MEV
items.prevention: Always include minAmountOut parameter. Let users set slippage tolerance.

items.title: Incorrect share calculations
items.description: Vault share math that allows rounding exploitation or share inflation.
items.impact: Value extraction through share manipulation
items.prevention: Use battle-tested ERC-4626 implementations. Add first depositor protection.

sections.heading: Token Handling Mistakes
sections.description: Errors in handling various token types.

items.title: Assuming all ERC-20s return bool
items.description: Not using SafeERC20 when some tokens (USDT) don't return bool on transfer.
items.impact: Transfers silently fail or revert unexpectedly
items.prevention: Always use SafeERC20 for ERC-20 interactions.

items.title: Not handling fee-on-transfer tokens
items.description: Assuming received amount equals transfer amount for tokens with transfer fees.
items.impact: Accounting errors, potential for exploitation
items.prevention: Calculate actual received amount via balance difference.

items.title: Ignoring token decimals
items.description: Assuming 18 decimals when USDC has 6 and others vary.
items.impact: Off by orders of magnitude in calculations
items.prevention: Query token decimals. Normalize all calculations.

items.title: Approval race condition
items.description: Approving new amount without resetting to zero first for tokens with approval race condition.
items.impact: Approved party can spend old + new allowance
items.prevention: Reset to zero first or use increaseAllowance/decreaseAllowance.

items.title: Not considering token blocklists
items.description: Ignoring that USDC/USDT can blocklist addresses, breaking protocol flows.
items.impact: Funds stuck if protocol address gets blocklisted
items.prevention: Have contingency for blocklist scenarios. Avoid holding stablecoins long-term.

items.title: Missing access control on critical functions
items.description: Administrative functions without onlyOwner or role checks.
items.impact: Anyone can call admin functions and drain or break protocol
items.prevention: Audit every external/public function. Default to restricted, explicitly open.

items.title: Single key controlling everything
items.description: One EOA can pause, upgrade, and withdraw all funds.
items.impact: Key compromise loses everything
items.prevention: Use multisig for admin functions. Separate roles for different operations.

items.title: No timelock on critical operations
items.description: Upgrades and parameter changes execute immediately without delay.
items.impact: No time for users to react to malicious changes
items.prevention: Add timelock for all critical admin operations.

items.title: Incorrect modifier ordering
items.description: Putting access control modifier after other checks allows bypass in some cases.
items.impact: Access control bypassed via early revert
items.prevention: Access control modifiers should be first in modifier chain.

proTips.tip: Study every DeFi exploit post-mortem. The patterns repeat with variations.
Get multiple audits from different firms. Each auditor catches different issues.
Deploy with low caps first. Increase limits gradually as protocol proves secure.
Have a bug bounty program. Ethical hackers finding bugs is better than malicious ones.
Build monitoring and alerts from day one. Fast response limits damage.
